task: Fix the log flood caused by a debug logger that was accidentally left active in production.

candidate_memories.content: Production log volume increased 40x after a debug logger was left active following an incident investigation.
The debug logger in processor/worker.go must be disabled by setting the log level back to INFO.
The debug logger was enabled manually via the admin API during the incident and was never reverted.
After an incident, always revert manual runtime configuration changes before closing the incident ticket.
The log flood is consuming 90% of the log aggregation quota; non-debug logs are being dropped as a result.
The logging infrastructure uses Fluentd to aggregate logs and forward them to Elasticsearch.
Session 6 note: the monitoring team added a log volume alert at 50% of the daily quota.
Old practice: debug logging was always on in early development; log levels were added in version 2.0.
The log aggregation quota is 500GB per day across all services.
Session 14 note: the SRE team documented the procedure for adjusting log levels via the admin API.
Old logging guide: the processor/worker debug logs were added during the race condition investigation in 2023.
All runtime configuration changes made during an incident must be added to the incident ticket as a remediation step.
Session 3 note: the logging format was changed from text to structured JSON.
The admin API for log level changes requires an ops role token and logs the change to the audit trail.
Session 10 note: the log search team added index retention policies to reduce storage costs.
Fluentd is configured with a buffer that can hold 30 minutes of logs before dropping.
Debug-level logging should never be enabled in production for more than 5 minutes without explicit monitoring.
Session 8 note: the security team added log masking for PII fields.
Old log guide: the worker log level was DEBUG during the initial deployment because log volumes were low.
Log archival to cold storage runs nightly; logs older than 30 days are compressed and moved to S3 Glacier.
